findings.title: Missing-directory case: the script still writes a manifest and exits 0.

findings.body:
**Check that a baseline unit count is a known integer before you sum it.**

Line 326 tests only `unit.count !== null`. An undefined count passes this test, and the sum at line 332 then becomes `NaN`. A string count such as `"3"` also passes, and the sum becomes the string `"03"`. In both cases the panel reports a corrupt denominator, not an unknown one. The comment at lines 302-305 says a unit counts only with a known count, so this breaks that rule. The corrupt value then crashes the renderer: `count()` in `scripts/measurement-rollup.mjs` (lines 114-119) throws on a non-finite or non-number value. A single malformed baseline row therefore aborts the whole readout.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      units.every((unit) => unit.completed === true && unit.count !== null);
+      units.every(
+        (unit) => unit.completed === true && Number.isSafeInteger(unit.count) && unit.count >= 0,
+      );
```
</details>

findings.body:
**`reviewOk` throws on a missing `initialBlocking` instead of rejecting the row.**

At line 72, `r.initialBlocking === null || r.initialBlocking.every(fingerprintOk)` fails when `initialBlocking` is absent. An undefined value throws a `TypeError`. A non-array value such as an object or a string also throws, because it has no `.every` method. The exception leaves `admit()` and stops `computeOutcomePanels` completely. The header (lines 4-5) says malformed evidence goes to the unknown list, and this crash breaks that rule. Every other field check in the validators guards the type first.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  (r.initialBlocking === null || r.initialBlocking.every(fingerprintOk)) &&
+  (r.initialBlocking === null ||
+    (Array.isArray(r.initialBlocking) && r.initialBlocking.every(fingerprintOk))) &&
```
</details>

findings.body:
**Restore the required policy rule check**

If a required rule is removed or renamed, `scripts/archive-measurement-evidence.mjs:30-38` silently omits it. Secret values that rely on that rule can then be stored and archived unredacted. The existing missing-rule test also expects the import to fail.

<details><summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
+const POLICY_SECRET_IDS = [
+  'class:route-key-material',
+  'class:token-ssh-plumbing',
+  'class:inline-secret-assignments',
+];
+const missingSecretIds = POLICY_SECRET_IDS.filter(
+  (id) => !policy.rules.some((rule) => rule.id === id),
+);
+if (missingSecretIds.length > 0)
+  throw new Error(
+    `measurement-bundle: policy/denylist/patterns.yml lacks required rule(s): ${missingSecretIds.join(', ')}`,
+  );
 const POLICY_SECRETS = policy.rules
-  .filter((rule) =>
-    [
-      'class:route-key-material',
-      'class:token-ssh-plumbing',
-      'class:inline-secret-assignments',
-    ].includes(rule.id),
-  )
+  .filter((rule) => POLICY_SECRET_IDS.includes(rule.id))
   .map((rule) => new RegExp(rule.regex, 'g'));
```

</details>
